summary: This is a Bankrate article by Sarah Foster, titled "6 key ways the Federal Reserve impacts your money" and published March 19, 2024. The clipped text contains the article's table of contents and author and site boilerplate, but the body text of the six sections is cut off, so the actual explanations are not in the note. The six listed topics are borrowing costs, loan qualification, savings yields, the stock market, purchasing power, and the job market.
one_line: Bankrate article by Sarah Foster (March 2024) outlining six ways Federal Reserve policy affects borrowing, savings, stocks, purchasing power and jobs.
key_facts: The article is titled "6 key ways the Federal Reserve impacts your money" and was published on March 19, 2024 by Bankrate.
The article is written by Sarah Foster, Principal U.S. Economy and Federal Reserve Reporter at Bankrate, and is edited by Lance Davis, Vice President of Content at Bankrate.
The article is listed as a 13 min read.
Its first section heading is "What does the Federal Reserve do?"
Section 1 is titled "The Fed influences borrowing costs."
Section 2 is titled "Higher rates make it harder to qualify for a loan."
Section 3 is titled "Savings yields move in lockstep with the Fed."
Section 4 is titled "Fed decisions guide the stock market."
Section 5 is titled "The Fed has a major influence on your purchasing power."
Section 6 is titled "The Fed impacts the job market."
Sarah Foster has covered the Federal Reserve and U.S. economy since 2018, when she joined the economics news team at Bloomberg News.
Bankrate was founded in 1976, according to the note.
The note states that over 100 million people depend on Bankrate as a trusted source of financial information every year.
Bankrate describes itself as an independent, advertising-supported comparison service.
Bankrate says it has partnerships with issuers including American Express, Bank of America, Capital One, Chase, Citi and Discover.
